newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Harvey Norman says Jan-Feb sales rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Harvey Norman says Jan-Feb sales rise.

text.p: Furniture and electrical goods retailer Harvey Norman Holdings Ltd said on Friday that total sales in the first two months of calendar 1997 had risen by 15 percent.

"The retail market in January and February continues to be difficult, however, the directors are pleased that Harvey Norman has weathered the retail market slump better than most," founder and chairman Gerry Harvey said in a statement accompanying the 1996/97 first half profit result.

The company said total sales in the first six months to December 31 rose 13.7 percent to A$601.86 million, consisting of its franchised "Harvey Norman" stores and from the company's own own store at Lismore on the north coast of the state of New South Wales.

"Sales from the franchised "Harvey Norman" stores and the economic entity's own store at Lismore for the period ended February totalled A$811.53 million, up 15.0 percent on the corresponding period for 1996," it said.
The first half sales result included contributions from two new stores in Queensland and one in Victoria, while the first New Zealand store in Auckland was expected to open in June 1997.
"During the second half of the financial year, the directors anticipate a positive contribution to profit from the newly opened stores ...", the company said.

First half operating profit rose by 2.6 percent to A$26.94 million while net profit rose by 8.4 percent to A$18.14 million, including an abnormal profit of A$1.61 million from the sale of shares in Freedom Furniture Ltd.
